chapters.title: Chapter 1: What a Central Bank Actually Does

lessons.title: Why Every Economy Needs a Central Bank

body.text: Money only works because millions of strangers trust it at the same time. A central bank exists to protect that trust: it keeps the value of the rupee stable, keeps the banking system standing when it wobbles, and steps in as the lender nobody else will be.

children.text: Every rupee in your Zerodha account, every salary credit, every UPI payment rests on an invisible promise. The promise is that the ₹500 you hold today will still buy roughly what it bought last month, and that the bank holding your savings will still be open tomorrow. In India, the institution responsible for keeping that promise is the
Reserve Bank of India
. This lesson explains why an economy cannot run without one, before we look at how the RBI actually does the job.
The Problem: Money Is a Confidence Game

markDefs.definition: Currency that has value because a government declares it legal tender and people trust it, not because it can be exchanged for gold or any physical commodity.

children.text: Modern money is
fiat money

. A ₹500 note is a piece of printed paper that costs a few rupees to make. It is worth ₹500 only because everyone accepts it at that value. If people start doubting it, the note loses value fast, and nothing physical stands behind it to stop the fall.
Leave money and banking entirely to private players and three problems show up again and again in history:
Too much money gets created.
Whoever issues money has a temptation to issue more of it, because new money is free spending power. The result is inflation that eats everyone else's savings.
Banks fail in chains.
Banks lend out most of the deposits they take. If depositors panic and all ask for cash together, even a healthy bank cannot pay. One failure triggers fear about the next bank.
Nobody manages the currency's external value.
A country that imports crude oil, electronics and gold needs foreign currency. Without someone managing reserves, a sudden shortage of dollars can freeze the economy.
A central bank is the institutional answer to all three.

body.title: Quick Check: What Gives a ₹500 Note Its Value?
body.question: Why is a ₹500 note worth ₹500 today?
options: The RBI holds ₹500 worth of gold in its vaults for every ₹500 note
It is legal tender and people trust that others will accept it at that value
The paper and ink used to print it cost close to ₹500
SEBI guarantees the value of every currency note
body.explanation: Indian currency is fiat money. Its value comes from legal tender status and collective trust. The RBI does hold gold as part of its reserves, but notes are not exchangeable for a fixed quantity of gold. SEBI regulates securities markets, not currency.

children.text: A Short History: Why Central Banks Were Invented
Central banks were not designed on a whiteboard. Almost every one was created after a crisis made the need painfully obvious.

body.title: How Central Banks Came to Exist

events.title: Sveriges Riksbank, Sweden
events.description: Generally recognised as the world's oldest surviving central bank, set up after an earlier private note-issuing bank collapsed.

events.title: Bank of England
events.description: Created to lend to the English government during war. Over the next two centuries it became the model for a bank that stands behind other banks in a panic.

events.title: US Federal Reserve
events.description: Established after the Panic of 1907, when a private banker, J.P. Morgan, had to personally organise a rescue of the US banking system. America decided that job needed a permanent public institution.

events.title: Reserve Bank of India
events.description: Began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. It started as a privately owned bank and was nationalised in 1949.

events.title: European Central Bank
events.description: Formed to run a single monetary policy for the countries adopting the euro, which launched in 1999.

body.text: Notice the pattern. The Fed was born out of a bank panic, and the Bank of England grew into its rescue role through repeated crises. Central banks exist because markets, left alone, periodically lose confidence all at once.

children.text: The Six Jobs of a Central Bank
Strip away the jargon and a central bank like the RBI does six things. Each one solves a specific failure you just read about.

body.caption: What the RBI Does, and Why It Matters to You

cells: Sole authority to issue banknotes in India (the Government of India issues coins)
The notes in your wallet and the cash your bank ATM dispenses
Sets the repo rate and manages liquidity to keep inflation near its target
Home loan EMIs, FD rates, and the valuations the Nifty trades at
Manages government accounts and runs the auction of government bonds
The G-Sec yields that debt mutual funds and your EPF returns depend on
Holds reserves of banks and lends to them overnight
Whether your bank has cash to lend to you
Licenses and inspects banks and NBFCs, and can restrict or rescue them
The safety of your savings account
Holds forex reserves and intervenes to smooth sharp moves in the rupee
The price of imported goods, foreign travel, and US stock investing

markDefs.definition: The role of a central bank in lending to solvent banks facing a sudden cash shortage, when no one else will lend to them, to stop a panic from spreading.

children.text: Of these, one role is the reason central banks exist at all: being the
lender of last resort
. When every private lender refuses to lend, the central bank still can, because it creates the rupees itself.

body.title: Name the Role
body.textWithBlank: When a sound bank faces a sudden rush of withdrawals and no private lender will help, the central bank steps in as the lender of ___ resort.
body.explanation: Lender of last resort. The central bank lends to solvent banks in a liquidity panic because it is the one institution that can never run out of its own currency.

children.text: Why a Bank Run Can Sink Even a Good Bank

markDefs.definition: A system where banks keep only a portion of deposits as cash or reserves and lend out the rest, so they can never repay all depositors at the same moment.

children.text: To see why the lender of last resort role matters, look at how a bank actually holds your money. Banks run on
fractional reserve banking
. They keep a slice of deposits as cash and reserves, and lend or invest the rest.

body.title: A Simplified Bank Balance Sheet: Where ₹100 of Deposits Goes

children.text: The split above is illustrative, but the logic is real. If ₹100 has been deposited and only about ₹8 sits as cash and reserves, the bank can comfortably handle normal daily withdrawals. It cannot handle everyone showing up on the same morning. The loans are real assets, but you cannot turn a 20-year home loan into cash by lunchtime.

markDefs.definition: A situation where many depositors withdraw money at once because they fear the bank will fail, which can cause the failure they fear.

children.text: That is a
bank run
: a panic that becomes self-fulfilling. The central bank breaks the cycle by lending cash against the bank's good assets, so depositors get paid and the panic dies.
India Case Studies: The RBI in Action
Yes Bank, March 2020

By late 2019, Yes Bank, then one of India's largest private sector banks, had seen its capital fall below regulatory requirements after heavy losses on stressed loans. Depositors were pulling money out.

body.title: The Yes Bank Rescue in 13 Days

events.title: Moratorium imposed
events.description: The government, on the RBI's application, placed Yes Bank under a moratorium. Withdrawals were capped at ₹50,000 per depositor and the RBI superseded the board.

events.title: Draft rescue plan
events.description: The RBI released a draft reconstruction scheme with State Bank of India as the lead investor bank.

events.title: Scheme notified
events.description: SBI took about 48% of the equity, with other private banks such as ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and Axis Bank also investing. SBI could not reduce its stake below 26% for three years.

events.title: Moratorium lifted
events.description: Withdrawal limits ended, well before the 30-day deadline. The bank kept operating and depositors did not lose their money.

body.text: Shareholders did not get the same protection as depositors. Yes Bank's share price had already collapsed on the NSE, and the rescue diluted existing shareholders heavily. A central bank protects the system and depositors. It does not protect your equity investment in a badly run bank.

children.text: PMC Bank, September 2019

Punjab and Maharashtra Co-operative Bank was found to have hidden large loans to one real estate group, HDIL. On 23 September 2019 the RBI placed it under directions and capped withdrawals at ₹1,000 per account. The limit was raised to ₹10,000 within days after depositor panic, and increased in steps after that. PMC was eventually absorbed by Unity Small Finance Bank.

body.title: Two Rescues, Two Very Different Experiences

columns.label: Yes Bank (2020)
points: Large private bank with systemic importance
Rescue capital arranged from SBI and other banks

columns.label: PMC Bank (2019)
points: Urban co-operative bank, under dual regulation at the time
Restrictions stretched on for well over a year
Resolved only through a merger into a new small finance bank

children.text: The lesson for an investor is simple. A central bank is a powerful safety net, but its speed and strength depend on how big and connected the failing institution is.

body.title: You Are a Depositor on 5 March 2020
body.scenario: Your salary account and a ₹3 lakh FD are both with Yes Bank. It is 5 March 2020, evening. News breaks of the moratorium and the ₹50,000 withdrawal cap. Your WhatsApp family group is flooded with messages saying the bank will shut and all money is gone. Your EMI of ₹32,000 is due on 10 March from this account.
body.prompt: What do you actually do in the next week, and what should you not do?
body.modelAnswer: First, separate the facts from the forwards. A moratorium is not a bank closure. The RBI imposed it precisely to protect depositors while a rescue is arranged, and your deposits are also covered by DICGC insurance up to ₹5 lakh. Second, handle the immediate cash need: you can withdraw up to ₹50,000, which covers the ₹32,000 EMI, or you can ask your lender to debit a different account this month. The moratorium had provisions for larger withdrawals in specific hardship cases such as medical treatment, education or weddings. Third, do not do anything irreversible out of panic, such as borrowing at high interest to cover expenses you can already meet. Finally, once things settle, diversify: keep your emergency fund and salary account in different banks so one bank problem never freezes all your money.

children.text: The Backstop Behind Your Savings: Deposit Insurance

markDefs.definition: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation, a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI that insures bank deposits in India.

children.text: Alongside the RBI sits the
DICGC
, a wholly owned RBI subsidiary. It insures deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, covering principal and interest together. This limit was raised from ₹1 lakh in February 2020.

body.label: Deposit insurance cover in India
body.context: Covers savings, current, fixed and recurring deposits together, including interest. It is counted separately for each bank you hold money with.

body.title: How Much of Your Money Is Uninsured?
body.prompt: Priya has an FD of ₹6,50,000 and a savings balance of ₹1,20,000, both with the same bank, in her own name. If the bank fails, how much of her money (in ₹) is NOT covered by DICGC insurance?
body.explanation: Total deposits = ₹6,50,000 + ₹1,20,000 = ₹7,70,000. Insurance covers ₹5,00,000 per depositor per bank, combined across account types. Uninsured amount = ₹7,70,000 minus ₹5,00,000 = ₹2,70,000. Splitting the FD across two different banks would have brought everything under cover.

children.text: Why Protecting Prices Matters as Much as Protecting Banks
Bank failures are dramatic. Inflation is quiet, and it does more total damage. If the central bank lets money grow much faster than the economy, prices rise and every rupee you have saved buys less.

body.caption: How much today's money will be worth in today's purchasing power after inflation

body.title: What ₹1 Lakh Kept as Cash Is Worth in Today's Money

children.text: The gap between those two lines is the entire case for an independent central bank that takes inflation seriously. At 8% inflation, cash loses more than half its value in 10 years. At 4%, it still loses about a third, which is exactly why cash sitting idle is never a real savings plan.

body.title: Calculate the Inflation Damage
body.prompt: You keep ₹1,00,000 in cash for 10 years. Inflation averages 6% a year. What is it worth in today's purchasing power? Round to the nearest rupee.
body.explanation: Real value = ₹1,00,000 ÷ (1.06)^10. (1.06)^10 is about 1.7908, so the real value is about ₹55,839. More than 44% of your purchasing power disappears, without a single rupee leaving your account.

body.title: Go Deeper: India's 1991 Crisis and the Gold That Left the Country

children.text: The third job, managing foreign exchange, sounds abstract until it fails. By mid 1991, after years of large fiscal and trade deficits and an oil price spike from the Gulf War, India's forex reserves had fallen to roughly three weeks of import cover.

To raise emergency funds, India pledged about 67 tonnes of gold as collateral in 1991: around 20 tonnes through SBI to Union Bank of Switzerland, and around 47 tonnes through the RBI with the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan. India also borrowed from the IMF. The gold was pledged, not sold, and was later reclaimed.

The crisis triggered the 1991 liberalisation reforms and permanently changed how the RBI thinks about reserves. Today it holds very large forex reserves specifically so a sudden dollar shortage never forces a repeat.

cards.definition: The public institution that issues a country's currency, sets monetary policy, supervises banks and manages forex reserves. In India, the RBI.
Money valued because it is legal tender and trusted, not because it is backed by a fixed amount of gold.
The central bank's role of lending to solvent banks in a panic when no one else will.
Mass withdrawals driven by fear of failure, which can bring down even a healthy bank.
A temporary legal freeze on a bank's operations and withdrawals, used to buy time for a rescue plan.
The RBI subsidiary that insures bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

body.title: Apply It This Week
steps: List every bank where you hold deposits and add up the total per bank, including FDs
Flag any bank where your total exceeds ₹5 lakh and decide whether to spread it
Check whether your emergency fund sits in the same bank as your salary account
Open the RBI monetary policy page and note the current repo rate
Look up the next MPC meeting date so you know when markets will be watching

points: Modern money is fiat money: it works only as long as people trust it, and a central bank exists to protect that trust.
Central banks were created after crises, because private systems repeatedly suffered runaway money creation, bank runs and currency shortages.
The RBI issues notes, sets monetary policy, banks for the government and for banks, regulates lenders and manages forex reserves.
The lender of last resort role stops a bank run from becoming a system-wide collapse, as the Yes Bank rescue in March 2020 showed.
Deposit insurance covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank. Equity shareholders of a failing bank have no such protection.
Unchecked inflation quietly destroys savings, which is why price stability sits at the heart of the RBI's mandate.

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not investment advice. Policy rates and figures are as of the RBI's August 2026 policy review and can change at any subsequent meeting.
